title: Tar index offset debugging notes
content:
Purpose:
Quick scratchpad for the model load failure we hit while serving model-x-v2 on dedicated: apparent mismatch between checkpoint index and tarball offsets. Recording commands, outputs, hypotheses, and next steps — mostly for myself and Maya.

Symptom summary:
- Serving process (runtime) crashed during weight map build while streaming shards from GCS.
- Error observed in logs: "Malformed TAR entry: size exceeds remaining object length (expected 1099511627776, got 18446744073709551615)" followed by "unexpected EOF while reading weights".
- Loading locally shows torch.unpickling.UnpicklingError when trying to open a weights file from the tar stream: "invalid load key, '\u001f'" (suggests gzip header on non-gzip expectation).

Files involved:
- gs://redwood-checkpoints/model-x-v2/weights-000.tar.gz (object served by GCS signed URL)
- gs://redwood-checkpoints/model-x-v2/index.json (manifest produced by packaging tool)
- runtime call: StreamTarReader -> TarIndexResolver -> WeightMapper

Commands I ran (local dev box, Debian 12):
1) Quick header inspection (raw):
   $ gsutil cat gs://redwood-checkpoints/model-x-v2/weights-000.tar.gz | head -c 512 | xxd -g 1 | head
   -> saw 0x1f 0x8b at offset 0 (gzip magic), but downstream code treats object as plain tar not gz.

2) Tar listing to check entries and sizes:
   $ gsutil cp gs://redwood-checkpoints/model-x-v2/weights-000.tar.gz /tmp/
   $ tar -tzvf /tmp/weights-000.tar.gz | head -n 40
   -> tar can list entries; sizes look reasonable but note: last entry size in listing mismatches index.json size for shard_11.pt

3) Compute sha256 of entire object and compare against index.json checksum (index has sha256):
   $ sha256sum /tmp/weights-000.tar.gz
   -> local sha256 differs from index.json (index claimed earlier build value). Possible stale index or partial re-upload.

4) Inspect index.json payload vs tar headers:
   $ jq -r '.files[] | "\(.name) \(.offset) \(.size) \(.sha256)"' index.json | head
   -> observed that offsets in index.json assume uncompressed tar positions (tar bytes), while file on GCS is compressed (gzip), so index offsets are wrong if index was computed before gz compression.

5) Confirm gzip vs plain tar hypothesis by attempting to gunzip stream and check tar offsets:
   $ gunzip -c /tmp/weights-000.tar.gz | tar -tvf - | head
   -> tar entries and sizes now line up with index.json offsets when interpreted relative to the uncompressed stream. That nails down mismatch: index computed pre-compression, we are using compressed object but runtime expects offsets into compressed object.

6) Repro to trigger runtime failure locally (simulate streaming reader expecting compressed offsets):
   - Run small python script to open tar.gz stream, seek to byte offset from index.json, and attempt to read header (fails because seeking on compressed stream doesn't map).

Error snippets captured:
- runtime.log:
  2026-02-19T14:03:12.442Z E model-loader: failed to open shard file shard_11.pt: tar header parse failure: invalid size field: 18446744073709551615
  2026-02-19T14:03:12.445Z E model-loader: unexpected EOF while streaming /model-x-v2/weights-000.tar.gz (read 124 bytes, expected > 10MiB)

- python unpickle test:
  >>> torch.load(fobj, map_location='cpu')
  UnpicklingError: invalid load key, '\u001f'

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Index was generated before gzip compression step; offsets are for raw tar file. Runtime is using compressed-object offsets (or vice-versa). Index and object are inconsistent due to packaging pipeline change.
2) Partial/overwritten upload: object on GCS has same name but content changed (compressed vs uncompressed) without regenerating index.
3) Client (runtime) has logic to support both compressed/uncompressed but auto-detection failed because content-type metadata was set incorrectly, forcing wrong codepath.
4) Corruption during upload (stream truncated) — less likely, since tar listing works but offsets mismatch.

Quick triage notes:
- Index JSON looks like it was produced by packaging script `make_tar_index.py` (see header comment). Packaging change history: check GH PRs around packaging tool (linked PR in artifacts).
- GCS object metadata currently: content-type=application/gzip, content-encoding absent, crc32c set. If runtime checks content-type first it should pick gzip path. But logs show it used tar-offsets not gzip streaming. Either metadata was not observed or code used a caller-specified format param.

Commands to fix / validate:
- If index was produced pre-gzip, either regenerate index on compressed file or re-upload uncompressed tar to match.
- Quick regeneration (on builder VM):
  $ gsutil cp gs://redwood-checkpoints/model-x-v2/weights-000.tar.gz /tmp/
  $ gunzip -c /tmp/weights-000.tar.gz > /tmp/weights-000.tar
  $ python tools/make_tar_index.py /tmp/weights-000.tar > index-fix.json
  $ jq -S . index-fix.json > index-fix.sorted.json
  # compare checksums and offsets to existing index.json

- If packaging pipeline must keep compressed objects for storage savings, update runtime to interpret offsets relative to compressed or to prefer streaming by name+filename rather than byte offsets. But streaming random-access into gzip is expensive; better to have index reflect compressed offsets if packaging uses block gzip (bgzip) or use separate smaller shard files.

Temporary mitigation deployed to dedicated pool (notes):
- Disabled indexed byte-range loading for model-x-v2 in rollout policy (fallback to whole-object stream, RAM permitting). This avoids incorrect seeks and allowed workers to warm up, but increases memory/IO.

Root cause candidate and recommended long-term fix:
- Root cause: packaging pipeline changed to gzip artifacts after index generation (CI order bug). The index generator runs on uncompressed tar, then CI gzips the object as final step without updating index. Hence offsets and checksums mismatch.
- Fix: reorder packaging CI steps so index is generated from final artifact, or update make_tar_index.py to accept gzipped input and emit compressed-offset index (hard/fragile). I prefer the former (generate index after compression to match bytes on GCS).

Next steps and owners:
- [Quinn] Draft PR to packaging CI to move index generation after gzip step. Include integration test that validates index offsets match served object by attempting to seek using range requests. Target: small release next week. (linked PR draft in artifacts)
- [Maya] Audit other checkpoint buckets for mixed compressed/uncompressed index mismatch (script: compare index sha256 vs object sha256).
- [Devin] Update runtime to log when content-type/encoding mismatches with index format to make future triage faster. Add warning when index offset > compressed object length.

Notes-to-self:
- If future artifacts need random access on compressed objects, consider using BGZF or storing uncompressed tar alongside compressed for backward compatibility.
- Keep copy of original uncompressed tar from this run at gs://redwood-checkpoints/archives/model-x-v2/weights-000.uncompressed.tar (uploaded locally as temporary backup during triage).

Attachments I saved locally:
- /tmp/weights-000.tar.gz (sha256: <redacted>)
- /tmp/weights-000.tar (gunzipped)
- index-fix.sorted.json (regenerated index on uncompressed)

Timestamps of important ops:
- 2026-02-19T13:48:03Z: alert fired from runtime group, model load failures began
- 2026-02-19T13:55:21Z: gsutil copy + initial header inspection
- 2026-02-19T14:20:12Z: staged mitigation (disabled indexed reads)

If anything else comes up I will append here. This doc is intentionally informal; aim is to capture breadcrumbs for later writeup.

-- quinn
